title: Julian Jaynes' bicameral mind theory: a shift in consciousness after 1000 BC
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Julian Jaynes' bicameral mind theory: a shift in consciousness after 1000 BC, about c. 1000 BC at ancient world, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: there's a guy named Julian James. I don't know if you've heard of him. He was a um Yale professor. He wrote a book called um uh on the origins of consciousness and the bicamal mind.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, brings up Julian Jaynes, whom he describes as a Yale professor who wrote a book called The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind. As Michels tells it, the theory says the human mind used to work in a split, two-part way and that consciousness as we know it took shape only after about 1000 BC. He raises it in a talk about the pyramids, because if true it would mean the ancient builders thought and experienced the world very differently from us.
